THE IDEA

A boundary learned, not drawn.

The network takes x and y coordinates between 0 and 1 and predicts a color. With two colors, it preserves the original single sigmoid output and threshold of 0.5. With 3–7 colors, it has one sigmoid output per color; the largest score wins. Training uses one-hot targets: 1 for the correct color and 0 for the others. Scores are not calibrated probabilities.

Try an experiment

  1. Start with Clusters and press Start training.
  2. Watch the loss fall and the decision map change.
  3. Choose up to 7 colors for Clusters or Circle. XOR uses two colors. Increase the learning rate to 0.3 to experiment with faster learning.
  4. Switch to Inspect and click the map to follow activations through the network.

Your original model, made interactive

The original 2–4–3–1 network, sigmoid activation, uniform −1 to 1 initialization, squared-error objective and backpropagation equations are preserved. Training samples with replacement, just as the original did. Seeded randomness and an adjustable learning rate make experiments reproducible.

Every dataset or architecture change resets the model and its history. Test points never update the weights. Small classes with fewer than 5 points have no held-out examples; accuracy on small datasets is noisy.

Everything runs on your device. Training stops at your chosen epoch target. You can increase it and continue with the learned weights. A run may settle into a poor solution; try a new seed or architecture. Refreshing the page starts a new experiment.

YOUR DATA

Bring your own points.

Paste or select a CSV with columns x,y,label. Coordinates must be 0–1 and integer labels 0–6. The number of colors expands automatically when needed. Use 2–1,000 rows. Importing replaces the current dataset and resets training.
